data.description:
## Description
**What**: Verify the per-language dynamic-import fail-open behavior of intent-header-source-check.sh for Python, JavaScript, and Ruby.
**Why**: Dynamic imports defeat static source-symbol matching; treating them as header_source_mismatch would produce false positives that erode trust in the signal. Fail-open with a warn keeps the check honest.
**Scope**:
- IN: detection and dynamic_import_inconclusive (warn) emission for Python importlib.import_module with a variable arg, JavaScript eval/Function/dynamic require with a computed string, and Ruby send/public_send; assertions that pre-commit does not block and the verifier surfaces these as informational (non-blocking) findings.
- OUT: the header-source check core logic (sc-3, draft-2); the broader nine-scenario e2e suite (sc-5, draft-4).

## Done Definitions

- For a Python test using importlib.import_module with a variable arg, a JavaScript test using eval/Function/dynamic require with a computed string, and a Ruby test using send/public_send, the check emits dynamic_import_inconclusive (warn) for each rather than header_source_mismatch ← Satisfies: sc-6
- On a test file emitting dynamic_import_inconclusive the pre-commit gate does not block and the completion-verifier renders the finding as informational (non-blocking) ← Satisfies: sc-6
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic ← Satisfies: sc-6

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Detection uses sg ast-grep patterns per language; when no parser exists for a language the same dynamic_import_inconclusive fail-open path applies with no grep fallback.
- [Dependency] Builds on intent-header-source-check.sh from draft-2; the per-language patterns extend that script's parse step.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO maintainer, I want per-language dynamic-import fail-open verification, so that tests using dynamic imports are warned rather than wrongly marked as mismatches.
